ranking.name: Forward-truth harness: real costs at the trade minute, permanent paper twins with known-dead controls, and the forward record of the frozen portfolio (the language model audits, reports and competes on paper only)
ranking.lens: adaptation + evidence (merged: League core, Three clocks cost logger, Sleeve factory core, Operating layer)
ranking.what_it_is: The eleven rules that already passed validation run every day on the broker's real quotes, each with a paper twin, next to eight rules the lab knows are dead and a coin-flip copy of each rule, which serve as lie detectors. The robot measures what a trade really costs at the exact minutes it trades (the open question on bitcoin and ether, 59 % of all trades) and keeps one running score of the whole portfolio that only counts days after the code was frozen. The language model never sends an order: it checks the journal every night, writes the evening phone report, and any 'AI as trader' idea gets a paper seat judged on future data only.
ranking.why_it_ranks_here: It is the only item resting on out-of-sample evidence (9 of 14 sleeves and 3 of 6 independent clusters passed validation, pooled z about 1.9), and the reviewers of two lenses converged on the same core: 'the forward-test harness that every later idea needs' and 'survives as a necessary module'. Its first answer is the cheapest and most decision-relevant of the panel: the crypto sleeves stand only 2.5 to 3.6 times above their modelled cost, the ether spread is known within a factor of four (1.16 to 4.32 USD), and 2 bp of extra cost puts the 72-hour bitcoin breakout at its pass bar; reading the real quotes settles that in days for nothing. It is immune by construction to the three things that sank everything else: the model's memory of past years, selection among 1,500 trials, and faster competitors. Ranks 2 to 5 are independent of it and can run the same week (about five days of work in all); it ranks first because each of them needs it before real money, and because it is what the user actually asked for. Weaknesses, stated plainly: it creates no edge of its own (35 % is the chance that the frozen portfolio keeps a real after-cost edge, at about half its validation level or better); the verdict on that edge takes 2.5 to 3 years at the validation level and ten or more at half; twins for ten more sleeves are 2 to 3 weeks of work, not days. Cut on the reviewers' objections: the nightly AI rule generator (about 6,200 trials a year at t >= 3 yields about 8 noise admissions, the same as its promised output), probation through a validation look, the on / half / off cost gate (unfalsifiable: about 196,000 trades to confirm its own claimed effect), yearly re-weighting, the live spread gate, and the yes / no language-model shadow arm (already answered by blind test 1).

First ten days on the FP demo to prove the plumbing (demo fills say nothing about cost); then real probes at minimum lot (0.01 gold and crypto, 0.1 us100) on each signal, closed within a minute while the twin carries the paper trade (a few tens of USD of spread in all). Slippage = fill minus requested price (stop orders) or minus the quote at send (market orders). Pass rules, fixed now: (a) at least 95 % of twin trades match the lab engine re-run on vendor data for the same days, else repair, and stop after two failed repairs; (b) signal count inside 270 +/- 33; (c) after 40 probes per instrument, the upper 95 % bound of spread + commission + slippage is within 1.5 x the model, else that instrument's sleeves go to paper; (d) the nightly reconciliation script (deterministic, not the language model) catches one seeded fault a month.

STEP 3 - the forward record (starts the day the twins are frozen; no extra work). x = each day's sum of R over the frozen sleeves at equal risk, from the twin ledger at measured cost. Score M = average of the two running products of (1 + k*x) for k = 0.01 and k = 0.02, both starting at 1. 'Edge confirmed' when M reaches 20: a worthless portfolio ever gets there at most 5 % of the time, however often the user looks. Expected wait: 2.5-3 years at the validation level (+0.079 R per trade), ten years or more at half. Everything to paper at -90 R from the peak or after a negative two-year total (1.7 % and 1 % likely with the edge, 29 % and 51 % without); nothing shorter than a quarter triggers anything; if the dead controls earn more than +0.03 R per trade after 2,000 paper trades, paper fills are too kind and every promotion is suspended. Risk per trade is fixed once at 0.25-0.5 %, or minimum lot where that is larger: about 2,500-3,000 EUR are needed for us100 and bitcoin, 8,000-11,000 EUR for the gold Donchian, so below that size 'only the percentage matters' is not true. The lead's planned single look at 2026 stays as written and can only kill: a zero-edge portfolio passes 'PF above 1' half the time.

STEP 4 - paper seats, forward only (after step 2 passes; 2-6 USD a month). No AI-written rule gets a validation look; a new seat needs a published mechanism, at most one new family a month, and is promoted on its own forward score only. First seats: (i) the plain 'data release 2 to 30 minutes before the gold breakout' flag, logged at no cost; (ii) the language model as cause reader: at each one-minute jump of at least 5 sigma on gold, us100 and eurusd (first of a 15-minute cluster, scheduled release minutes excluded) one call labels the rows of the public squawk page https://t.me/s/financialjuice stamped before jump + 90 s; no order is sent. One test, read once at 500 events in the class or 150 distinct days, whichever comes later (about two years): the class 'confirmed, new, material, and explains the direction' earns more than zero net over the next 60 minutes (entry at the first bar opening at least 120 s after the jump, real bid / ask) with p <= 0.01 against labels shuffled by day, stays positive without its five best days, and beats the keyword flag by at least 2 bp. Fail = the reader is switched off and the prompt is not rewritten.

ranking.name: Month-end London fix reversal on six dollar pairs (one frozen rule, one validation look)
ranking.what_it_is: On the last business day of each month, funds that hedge their US shares must trade dollars at the 16:00 London benchmark whatever the price, and the direction is known the day before from whether the S&P 500 rose or fell that month. The robot takes the other side at 16:02 London on six dollar pairs and closes at 16:30, when the pressure has lifted and the price comes back. It is one dollar bet a month, lasting 28 minutes.
ranking.why_it_ranks_here: Highest odds of a new, independent edge in the panel, and the reviewer tried to break it and could not: +3.75 bp net on 108 month-ends (t 4.8, 73 % of dates positive), every year 2013-2021 positive, still +3.4 bp without its five best dates, the same trade on other days or hours is flat or negative, other ways of choosing the sign fail, gross is 4.7 times the cost and survives a tripling, and entry at 16:01 or 16:02 is as good as 16:00, so the user's latency is enough. The flow is documented independently (Melvin and Prins 2015). The test is the cleanest on offer: one day, no language model (so no memory leak), a pass rule that chance satisfies under 3 % of the time, and validation years that have only been opened on currencies for an unrelated 4-hour trend transfer on three pairs, never at the fixing minutes. It ranks below the harness on fit and size: twelve bets a year, about +0.5 % per month-end in sample at 2 % risk (plan on about 3 % a year), no AI, nothing for 'several trades a day'; as an independent stream it would still be a real diversifier. Weak points kept inside the test design: the 'sell dollars in down months' half rests on 7 dates of 2019-2021 (-0.26 bp on the 19 down months of 2013-2018); the edge sits in a three-minute band (16:05 keeps half, 16:07 almost nothing); the lab frame shows no spread widening at the month-end fix, which a retail feed may not confirm; trade press reports funds delivering these orders earlier since 2023; six windows were looked at and the yen was dropped after seeing it flat.

ranking.name: Stressed-market gate on the us100 noise-area momentum sleeve (dealer-gamma flag and price-only flag, one validation look, 1.5x / 0.75x sizing)
ranking.what_it_is: Each morning before the US open the robot checks two public numbers: whether option dealers' gamma on the S&P 500 is in the lowest third of the past year, and whether the S&P 500's last five days are in their worst third. On such stressed days hedgers have to trade with the move, intraday trends on the Nasdaq run further, and the existing momentum rule is run at 1.5 times its normal risk; on calm days at 0.75 times. It adds no trade; it changes how much is bet each day.
ranking.why_it_ranks_here: The cheapest experiment of the panel (half a day) on the user's core intraday sleeve, and the only ranked idea that really changes behaviour day by day. The in-sample regime dependence looks real: the tercile gap is +0.14 R (z 2.6), a circular-shift permutation gives p = 0.0025, gamma lagged 60 days shows nothing, and the 840 trades taken when neither flag is on earn exactly 0.000 R; the direction agrees with published work (index intraday momentum only when dealers' net gamma is negative). It is third because the reviewer's objections are only partly answered. A price-only variable (S&P 5-day return) reproduces the split (z 2.65) and gamma adds nothing once the recent drawdown is in the regression, so the 'option positioning' story is unproven: the adopted variant therefore tests both flags as a 'stressed market' gate and prefers the price-only one. The effect is reversed on the other us100 sleeve, weaker on us500 and reversed in 2021; ten of 410 low-gamma days supply half the profit. The look is a second look at a sleeve whose own validation t is 1.89, and 2022 is widely known as a stressed, trending year, so it is not perfectly blind. The prize is modest: about +20-30 % risk-adjusted on one sleeve of eleven, no new trade. Hence a pass buys only a 1.5x / 0.75x tilt (about -6 % if the flag is noise, against -18 % for the designer's 2x / 0.5x) and moves belief from about 25 % to about 60 %.

ranking.name: Tokyo fixing on settlement days: sell USD/JPY at 09:55 Tokyo, cover at 11:55 (gotobi days only)
ranking.what_it_is: On Japanese settlement days (the 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th and month-end) banks buy dollars for importers whose orders are priced at the 09:55 Tokyo fixing, which pushes USD/JPY up into that minute. Once the flow is done the price tends to fall back over the next two hours. The robot sells USD/JPY at 09:55 Tokyo time on those days and buys back at 11:55, about six times a month.
ranking.why_it_ranks_here: The flow itself is the best-verified mechanism in the panel: on 2,152 Japanese working days the run-up into 09:55 is +0.98 bp (t 5.7) and the ten-minute fall after it +0.88 bp (t 6.6); on 124 Japanese bank holidays both vanish; on settlement days they double; 09:55 ranks first of 288 start times; there is a peer-reviewed prior (Krohn, Mueller and Whelan, Journal of Finance 2024); no language model is involved; the data is in the lab and USD/JPY validation has never been opened at these minutes. It is fourth because what is left after this account's costs is thin. The every-weekday version is cut: 63 % of its trades net about zero. The settlement-day version nets +1.96 bp (t 2.3, 8 of 9 years) once the commission is modelled correctly (the lab frame understates the USD/JPY cost by about 0.22 bp), which is below the lab's own in-sample bar of t 2.5, so the first step may end it. Only the first ten minutes are fixing flow; the other +1.3 bp of the two-hour hold also appears on holidays and resembles a yen drift the lab already rejected. The ten-minute fall shrank from about 1.1 to 0.7 bp between 2013-2017 and 2018-2021, the trade is standard fare for Japanese retail traders who pay about a seventh of this user's cost, and the prize is 1-2 % a year per 1x notional. One day of work that reuses the month-end rule's calendar and clock code: worth the test, not more.

The story does not match the trades: every entry falls between 06:00 and 11:59 UTC, where there is no US release, and the designer's own large replication on 14,245 currency breakouts shows a gap of 0.03 R. The validation step is not decisive (it passes 18 % of the time with no effect, 49 % with a true gap of 0.20 R), the size tilt has negative expected value below 39 % belief, the gold sleeve's validation has already been read many times, and it adds no trade. Kept only as a free log column in the harness (rank 1): no validation look, no tilt, no language-model stage.

dropped.name: Reader on unscheduled news as a trading sleeve: follow a jump when the model finds confirmed, new, material news (information)
dropped.why: Its first experiment cannot see its own effect: a class of 80 events has a standard error near 5 bp, about 10 % power for the 4-5 bp edge it hopes for. In sample the profit is ten historic days (+6.7 bp falls to +1.5 bp, t 1.1, without them), and the lab's own post-cut-off test shows the Nasdaq move is over before 'post + 2 minutes'. Dead as a sleeve (reviewer: 2 %). Kept only in the reviewer's form, as a no-order paper seat inside rank 1 with one properly powered test in about two years.

dropped.name: The League's nightly AI rule generator and probation through a validation look (adaptation)
dropped.why: Its output rate equals its false-positive rate: about 6,200 new trials a year at t >= 3 give about 8 noise admissions and 1-2 noise probation seats a year, exactly the 'few seats a year' promised. The 2022-2025 look is not out of sample for a rule written by a model that knows those years. The only conclusive test takes 18-24 months at 25-31 % power, and quarter-size seats need an account of 8,000-11,000 EUR. The forward-dated core is kept as rank 1.

dropped.name: Three clocks: on / half / off cost gate, shrinkage weights and risk halving after a negative calendar year (adaptation)
dropped.why: No experiment can fail: the gate's own claimed effect (-0.005 to +0.01 R per trade) needs about 196,000 trades to confirm, its ratio rests on validation expectancies whose standard error is as large as themselves, the calendar-year halving fires 22 % of years with the edge at half strength against 50 % with none (2.3 to 1 is not evidence), and it asks for two more validation looks. Kept inside rank 1: cost logging at signal time with the single 1.5x envelope rule, one fixed bet size, one drawdown rule.

dropped.name: Sleeve factory: expansion batches of 20 hypotheses with up to 4 validation shots each (evidence)
dropped.why: The 'next batch' is mostly refuted already: the gold trend rule on oil scored PF 0.60 (t -3.19) in validation, silver nets PF 0.73-0.98 after costs, the us100 rules fail on us500 and us30, four frozen transfers on eight currency pairs give PF 0.92-0.98, the opening rules fail on shares; the last eight tracks (about 580 configurations) added at most one sleeve. 'At least 2 passes of 4' happens 14-25 % of the time with no edge, and every batch re-spends the same 2022-2025 window. The core (the frozen portfolio judged on forward data) is rank 1.

dropped.name: Operating layer: live spread gate and the paper shadow league of a yes / no language-model judge and a ridge scorecard (evidence)
dropped.why: The spread gate cannot be judged by its own rule (200 skipped entries take about four years) and is dangerous on trend sleeves whose best 5 % of trades carry 169-206 % of the profit. The yes / no judge repeats blind test 1 (6,174 signals, negative) on a sixth of the sample; the scorecard's own expected z is 0.7-1.6 against a bar of 2.5. The cited fleet study concerns language-model agents on memecoins, not a rule robot. Kept inside rank 1: reconciliation, real-fill slippage measurement, the evening report.

dropped.name: Gamma gate on a second us500 sleeve (flows)
dropped.why: The same bet as us100, weaker in sample (+0.094 R on low-gamma days), and it only adds highly correlated trades.

dropped.name: Tokyo fixing every weekday, and the two-trade version long 09:30-09:55 then short to 10:30 (house, flows)
dropped.why: Every weekday: the 1,379 trades that are neither settlement days nor Fridays net +0.24 bp (t 0.5) at the corrected cost; the profit is settlement days, Fridays and a few yen safe-haven days (1 % of days make three quarters of the total). Two-trade version: both legs hang on the single 09:55:00 quote; one minute off, the pair nets about 0.8 bp against 1.5 bp of cost.

dropped.name: JP225 noise-area leg, HK50 and AUS200 (breadth)
dropped.why: The noise-area rule earns +2.9 bp gross against a 1.6-3.6 bp round trip (net t 0.8-1.2; ten days make 82 % of the gross total). HK50 costs 3.5-8 bp at other brokers and AUS200 1.1-3.4 bp against a small expected edge; neither was tested.

dropped.name: Small-cap leg: US2000 with the two frozen us100 rules (breadth)
dropped.why: Dead on its own terms: the free history starts on 2019-03-20, so 2.8 in-sample years cannot reach t 2.5 even at us100 strength; the noise-area rule loses before costs (-6.7 bp per trade, t -2.5, negative in all three years); the idea's own spanning test against the us100 sleeves has a negative intercept (t -2.2 to -2.5 after costs); the cost is 2-3 times that of us100.

verdict.what_ai_is_for:
Where AI does not give this user an advantage (the lab, the outside literature and this panel agree):
1. Deciding trades. Three pre-registered blind tests are negative: as a yes / no judge on 6,174 signals it kept +0.061 R and threw away +0.076 R; trading 1,000 gold charts freely it made -0.086 R, the same as its answers shuffled; reading 2,147 presidential posts it lost 5.8 bp per call, the price having moved before 'post + 2 minutes'. Gradient boosting on prices is right 51-56 % of the time where 55-75 % is needed. Outside the lab, live contests and fleets of language-model traders lose or show no directional edge, and published 'AI-discovered' strategies vanish once memory of the test period and the number of trials are controlled. In this panel the two ideas that put the model's reading into the decision were given 2 % and 4 % by their own reviewer, and every idea with after-cost support has no language model in the decision.
2. Speed. A call takes 3-30 seconds; the news is in the price within two minutes.
3. Learning direction day by day. An edge of +0.05 to +0.10 R per trade against a scatter of 1.4 R needs roughly 800 to 3,000 trades (one to several years) to be told from zero. Every fast adaptation checked in sample (chasing recent winners, bandits, volatility-state sizing, cutting after losses) did no better than equal weights.
4. Mass-producing rules. After 1,500 trials the best pure-noise rule already shows t = 3.35; the last eight research tracks (about 580 configurations) added at most one sleeve, and a nightly generator would admit about as many noise rules as real ones.

Where AI does give him a real advantage:
1. Research labour with discipline, which a lone retail trader cannot afford: about 1,500 configurations tested at his own account's costs under rules written in advance, and half a dozen good-looking rules stopped before they cost money (the FOMC rule, the oil transfer at PF 0.60 in validation, short VIX, dip-buying). In this panel alone the reviewers reproduced the designers' numbers and caught a 0.22 bp cost error on USD/JPY that pushes one candidate below the lab's own bar, missing opening bars in the Japanese data, a small-cap history too short to ever pass, a plain price series that reproduces the 'gamma' effect, and a news story whose releases fall outside the trading window.
2. Reading. Every validated sleeve and every ranked candidate is a published flow or hedging effect, found in the literature and re-tested at his costs. The 'new eye' that worked is asking who is forced to trade and when, not asking a model where the price goes.
3. Engineering and supervision: MQL5 code with Python twins, nightly reconciliation, calendars (holidays, settlement-day shifts, exchange-hour changes), each mismatch explained and the evening note written in plain French, for under 20 USD of his 200 USD a month. The budget is not the limit; the statistics are.
4. Being tested honestly as a trader, on paper and on future data only, at 2-5 % odds over about two years.

So 'AI at 100 %' is true of the research, the engineering and the supervision, and should stay at 0 % of the order decision until a forward paper record says otherwise. 'Adapts day by day' can honestly mean three things: costs and fills re-measured continuously (weeks), one daily market-state switch if it passes its single test, and a roster of rules that changes by quarters and years.
verdict.summary_fr:
Verdict du jury : trois pistes sérieuses.

1. Le banc de vérité : vos onze règles validées tournent sur les vrais prix du courtier, on mesure leurs frais réels (surtout bitcoin et ether), l'IA contrôle chaque nuit et écrit votre rapport du soir. Chance que ce portefeuille gagne vraiment : une sur trois environ. Preuve complète : deux à trois ans.

2. Fin de mois sur les devises : une fois par mois, vers 17 h, parier que le dollar revient après les ordres forcés des grands fonds. Une chance sur trois ; réponse en un jour.

3. Nasdaq : miser plus gros les matins de marché sous tension. Une chance sur quatre ; réponse en une demi-journée.

Deux pistes japonaises suivent, plus fragiles.

Franchement : rien ne promet un gain chaque jour. L'IA ne choisit aucune position, ses trois tests à l'aveugle ont échoué : elle cherche, vérifie, code et surveille.

ideas.name: News-backed breakout: full risk only on breakouts that fresh information started
ideas.pitch: A break of the overnight range that happens minutes after a real data release tends to keep going for a day or two; the same break in a news vacuum is mostly noise. A reader checks a time-stamped headline tape when the already validated gold breakout rule fires, and the robot puts full risk only on the news-backed breaks.
ideas.mechanism: Other side: short-term traders and liquidity providers who fade a break of the Asian range. When the break is caused by new information (a release that moves the dollar and yields), slower money finishes the move over the next 24-48 hours (asset managers and trend funds scaling in, hedgers, the next time zone) and the faders are stopped out; when nothing happened the break is a stop run and comes back. Speed desks take the first seconds of the release, which is not what is traded here: in-sample the advantage is intact for entries 2 to 30 minutes after the release, and the payoff is 38 % winners with a few large ones held about 30 hours, unattractive to fast players and irrelevant in size. In-sample evidence (2014-2021, plain tape, exploratory: about 50 cells were examined, so a single t of 2.4 is weak): gold Asian-range sleeve, 914 trades. Entered 2-30 min after a data post: +0.39 R (n 287, 37.6 % winners, +0.22 R without the 5 best trades). No data post in the previous 30 min: +0.004 R (n 591). Difference t 2.4, news-backed better in 7 of 8 years. The effect fades with distance from the release (2-10 min +0.66 R, 10-30 +0.25, 30-90 +0.08, 90-240 -0.12). The same flag read one day earlier at the same clock time (placebo) gives 0.00 on the gold sleeves. Entries inside the first 2 minutes were excluded to rule out a fill artefact. Counter-evidence: central-bank headlines alone do nothing; no split at all on the two us100 momentum sleeves or on bitcoin-follows-Nasdaq; the split on the crypto hourly breakouts (+0.20 R) is matched by its previous-day placebo (+0.16 R), so it is clock and regime, not news; on 14,245 in-sample FX London-open breakout trades the difference has the right sign but is negligible (-0.020 R vs -0.047 R, t 1.2).
ideas.role_of_ai: Stage A, no language model: a script polls the tape, a regular expression recognises a data release (headline of the form 'X vs Y expected'), and the robot checks whether one was published 2-30 minutes before the breakout fill. This is the part with in-sample support and it needs no AI. Stage B, the language model: one call per breakout signal (3-5 a day over all breakout sleeves, about 150 calls and 3 USD a month; a 3-30 second answer is harmless on a 30-hour trade). It reads the last 60 minutes of tape and answers three closed questions: is there fresh information behind this move, including unscheduled items a regular expression cannot recognise; does it point in the direction of the break; is it confirmed or a rumour. It never forecasts price, it certifies a cause. Stage B can only be measured on signals after 2026-06-30 and forward on demo.
ideas.instruments: XAUUSD first: the validated Asian-range breakout held two days. The 4-hour Donchian gold sleeve shows the same sign, weaker (+0.31 R vs +0.08 R, t 1.95). Then, as a new in-sample rule family, session-range breakouts conditioned on a data post for us100, ger40, oil and btcusd. Not FX (the replication there is negligible).
ideas.trades_per_day: It adds no trades. The gold sleeve fires about 0.46 times a day (116 a year), of which about 36 a year are news-backed. Used as a size tilt (for example 1.5 x on news-backed, 0.5 x on the others) the trade count is unchanged. A wider family over five markets might reach 0.5-1 a day; that is unproven.
ideas.holding_time: Unchanged from the sleeve: median 30 hours, maximum two days.
ideas.edge_vs_cost: In-sample, news-backed gold breaks earn +0.39 R net; one R is a 50 bp stop, so about +20 bp per trade against a 1.1 bp round trip, while the other 65 % of the sleeve's trades earn about zero. Expect at least half of that gap to be selection. A realistic hope is +0.15 to +0.25 R more on a third of the trades, i.e. the sleeve's profit per unit of risk rising by a third to a half; it is a quality filter, not a new source of profit. Cost is not the issue (10-20 x cost if real); the issue is whether the split is real.
ideas.data_needed: Free. investingLive weekly sitemaps, https://investinglive.com/sitemaps/news/articles/YYYY-Wnn.xml, 2010 to today, headline in the URL, publication time to the second (data posts appear a median 8-10 s after the release); the 418 weekly files for 2014-2021 download in one minute. The URL format changes at the end of November 2021 (no '!/' and no date suffix), so the parser needs a second pattern for 2022 onwards. Live: the same site plus https://t.me/s/financialjuice. Trades: the frozen files already in /home/user/gold-orb/lab/results/r2/recalc/trades. No price download.
ideas.first_experiment: Step 1 (2 days, 0 USD, in-sample only): freeze the flag exactly as I tested it (headline slug matches '-vs-|expected|estimate|prior', published 2-30 min before the entry) and redo the check inside the lab engine on the gold sleeves, every-signal runs and costs x1.5 included. This is confirmation, not evidence: gap news-backed minus the rest at least +0.25 R, previous-day placebo below +0.10 R. Step 2 (lead only, one look, written down first): validation 2022-2025 on the gold Asian-range sleeve, about 450 trades of which about 140 news-backed. Pass if news-backed mean R > 0, gap at least +0.15 R, and news-backed better in at least 3 of the 4 years. Honest power: the standard error of that gap is about 0.25 R, so a pass is moderate evidence and a pass by pure chance is roughly 1 in 7. That is why the use is a size tilt (a wrong tilt adds variance, it does not remove expectancy) and why news-backed versus the rest is then logged live. Step 3 (2 days): the same condition as a new rule family, at most 30 configurations, on us100, ger40, oil, btcusd under the usual criteria. Step 4 (1 day, about 5 USD): language-model labels on the roughly 230 breakout signals of July-November 2026, compared with the plain flag.
ideas.kill_rule: Stop if step 1 does not reproduce in the engine (gap below +0.25 R on every-signal trades with costs x1.5, or the placebo reaches half of the effect). Stop for good if the validation gap is zero or negative: no second definition of the flag, no other window. The language-model stage is dropped if, after 200 labelled signals, its 'news-backed' class does not separate trades better than the plain regular-expression flag.
ideas.differs_from_failed: The failed macro-release rules bought before or at a release; here nothing is traded on the release, it only filters a price rule that already passed validation. The failed yes/no judge saw anonymised numbers and no news; this gate uses exactly the information that test left out, and its first version is a script, so it can be checked on 2014-2025 with no memory leak. The failed opening-range breakouts were unconditional; the claim here is narrower: the Asian-range break is only worth full risk when information started it.

ideas.name: Reader on unscheduled news: follow a jump only when confirmed, new, material news is found behind it
ideas.pitch: When gold, oil or an index jumps, the model reads the last minutes of a free news squawk and says whether real, confirmed, new information explains the move; the robot follows only those jumps for up to an hour and ignores jumps caused by rumours, recycled headlines or nothing. The market supplies the direction and the size, the model only names the cause.
ideas.mechanism: Published work on index funds finds that jumps tied to unscheduled news tend to continue while no-news and scheduled-news jumps revert (Xiao, Yin, Zhao 2020), and that news needing interpretation is absorbed slowly (Lopez-Lira and Tang 2025; Jiang, Li, Wang 2021). Other side: market makers and range traders who lean against a jump they cannot explain, and keyword algorithms that handle scheduled numbers but not 'what does this mean'. Speed desks own the first seconds; what remains is paid for sitting through a messy hour with a coin-flip hit rate. My in-sample check with a crude keyword reader (2014-2021, six markets, one-minute jumps of at least 5 sigma, entry 1-2 minutes later, gross): jumps with a political or geopolitical headline at the jump earn +4.1 bp at 15 min and +6.7 bp at 60 min (n 1,300 on 606 days, t by day 2.5 and 2.8); central-bank headlines -0.4 / -1.2; data headlines about 0; no headline +0.2 / +0.1. But only 50 % of these trades win, and without the 10 best days of 609 (Brexit night, March 2020, vaccine Monday) the 60-minute result falls to about +1.5 bp per trade (t 1.1), roughly the cost; on each market the profit disappears without its 5 best days. Jumps on 'sources say / report' headlines continue only 42 % of the time (a fade wins 58 % but earns about 1.5 bp before costs). So the plain version is a rare-big-day harvest of the kind the lab's trend sleeves already collect; the open question is whether a real reader isolates a class that pays on ordinary days.
ideas.role_of_ai: Plain algorithm: detects the jump (one-minute move of at least 5 sigma, first of a 15-minute cluster, not a scheduled release minute), collects the tape rows time-stamped before the decision (jump + 90 s), places and manages the order. Language model: one call per jump (3-10 a day, 20-30 s, well inside the budget). It reads those rows plus a digest of the last 24 hours and returns a closed label (confirmed-new-material / unconfirmed report / repeat of known news / routine / nothing found) and whether the item explains the direction of the move. The hope is that it beats keywords on the three judgments that need reading: is it confirmed, is it new, does it matter for this market. It does not predict.
ideas.instruments: XAUUSD, WTI oil, US100, GER40, EURUSD, USDJPY (the six markets of the in-sample check; oil showed the largest effect, +17 bp at 60 min, and has the widest spread).
ideas.trades_per_day: With keywords: 165 a year over the six markets (0.65 a day), bunched on about 77 days a year because one headline moves several markets at once. With a denser tape and the model perhaps 1-1.5 a day on news days and none on quiet days.
ideas.holding_time: 15 to 60 minutes; stop at about 1.5 x the size of the jump; flat after 60 minutes.
ideas.edge_vs_cost: In-sample gross per trade at 60 minutes: oil +16.8 bp (cost about 5), GER40 +7.7 (1-1.5), US100 +5.5 (0.8), gold +4.9 (1.1), EURUSD +2.9 (0.85), USDJPY +2.6 (1-2). Pooled +6.7 bp gross, about +5 bp net ON AVERAGE, but the median trade earns zero and without ten historic days in eight years the net is about zero. Spreads one to two minutes after a jump are 1.5-3 x normal, which the test must charge from the real bid/ask. For the idea to be worth anything, the model's 'confirmed-new-material' class must earn at least 4 bp net with its five best days removed; nothing I measured says it will.
ideas.data_needed: Free and checked today: FinancialJuice public Telegram page (about 26,000 posts from 2026-07-01 to 2026-11-10, stamped to the second, about 1,300 pages to fetch), investingLive sitemaps, the presidential-post archive already in the lab. One-minute bid/ask for July-November 2026: gold, us100 and eurusd are already in lab/data/llm/news/px; oil, ger40 and usdjpy would be downloaded for this test only (lead's decision, as for the news test).
ideas.first_experiment: Post-cutoff only: 2026-07-22 to 2026-11-10 (the first three weeks of July are used to write the prompt and are excluded). About 1,200 jumps expected over the six markets (in-sample rate about 3,300 a year). One frozen prompt, one batch run, about 15-25 USD, four days of work. Scoring identical for every event: entry at the open of the first minute bar starting at least 120 s after the jump bar began, at the real bid/ask plus slippage; exit 60 minutes later (15 minutes secondary). One pre-registered primary test: the class 'confirmed-new-material and explains the direction' has a mean net return above zero with p <= 0.01 against 5,000 shuffles of the labels within market, AND stays above zero with its five best days removed, AND beats the plain keyword flag on the same events. Fewer than 80 events in the class = inconclusive. Reported only, never promoted: 'unconfirmed report' jumps faded; each market; each month.
ideas.kill_rule: If any leg of the primary test fails, the sleeve is dropped and the prompt is not rewritten for a second try. If inconclusive (fewer than 80 events), continue on demo until 150 events and apply the same rule. Even on a pass it stays on demo at minimum size until 150 live events confirm.
ideas.differs_from_failed: In the presidential-post test the model chose the direction from the text and the trade was taken whatever the market did; the move was over within two minutes. Here the market's own jump supplies direction and importance, the model only certifies the cause, scheduled releases are excluded, and the source is a full squawk instead of one author. It is neither a fade nor a release-timing rule. It is still a language-model-reads-news idea, and the lab's three negative tests are the right starting belief.

dropped_by_designer: Earnings releases / call text against the opening gap on US share CFDs: Lopez-Lira and Tang (version of Oct 2025, sample 2021-2024) find earnings news fully priced in the initial reaction (drift term -4.7 bp, not significant); what drifts is complex news in small caps, the strategy's Sharpe fell from 6.5 to 1.2 between 2021 and 2024 and it loses money at 20 bp round trip, while share CFDs cost 8 bp or more plus a minimum commission.

Language-model cause filter on 'bitcoin follows a Nasdaq impulse': in-sample, bitcoin's 60-minute follow-through is the same with a headline on the tape (+8.5 bp) as without (+6.9 bp), and the same across clock buckets and across 'gold or the euro jumped too' proxies; the cause does not matter.

Fading unexplained (no-news) jumps on us100, gold, EURUSD: in-sample the reversal (us100 -1.6 bp in 15 min, t -2.1) exists only when 'no headline for the next ten minutes' is known in hindsight; with what is known at decision time it is +0.1 bp.

Post-release drift after scheduled data, using the tape as a free calendar: in-sample the us100 'continuation' (+6.4 bp in 60 min) is one-sided, +11 bp after up-moves and -0.3 bp after down-moves; it is the release-day long drift that already failed validation.

Overnight gap 'explained by news continues, unexplained gap fills' on us100 and GER40: in-sample, tape intensity does not split gaps; big gaps after a busy night reverse in the first hour (-16 bp, n 90, t -2.1), the opposite sign and only 11 cases a year.
News-backed gate on the crypto hourly breakouts: in-sample split of +0.20 R, but the same flag taken one day earlier does as well (+0.16 R): time of day and regime, not news.
'Information day' gate for the us100 intraday-momentum sleeves: tape flags separate nothing (0.00 R), and the lab's own events table shows intraday momentum negative on release days.

FX option-expiry 'magnets' read from the public trade repository (free files verified back to January 2025) or the daily expiry posts: the Swiss National Bank working paper 2019-03 rebuilds dealers' positions from the same data and finds them short gamma on average, so hedging amplifies moves instead of pinning them; the sign is ambiguous and the measured effect tiny.

Prediction markets as an information feed for oil and gold (Polymarket minute history is free and reachable): the documented informed bets came 71 minutes to a few hours before the news and the big cases fell on Saturdays (Iran strike of 28 Feb 2026, Maduro) when CFDs are closed; profit is an input of the published flag, enforcement started in February 2026, and only a handful of tradable events occur a year, so it cannot be falsified.

Other-language-first news for JP225, HK50, GER40, USDJPY (Japanese central-bank and political scoops, Chinese cabinet and commerce-ministry notices, German ad-hoc disclosures): local desks and bilingual wire reporters relay within about a minute, and there are 10-40 usable events a year per market.

Long scheduled documents against the first reaction (FOMC minutes, ECB accounts, court rulings, tariff annexes): 8-30 events a year, reporters under embargo and funds running their own language models are faster; several years would be needed to find out it does not work.

Watching obscure public documents (Federal Register pre-publication desk, customs rulings as in the August 2025 gold-bar case, exchange margin notices): real but a few unique events a year; an alert service, not a statistical robot.
Central-bank stance tracker and daily news-sentiment direction for indices and currencies: published effects are a few basis points a day at one decision a day; untestable in less than several years.
Reacting faster to presidential posts: the lab's own test shows the move is over before post + 2 minutes; competing on seconds is not this user's game.

reviews.name: News-backed breakout: full risk only on breakouts that fresh information started
reviews.fatal_flaw:
The split is most likely the best of about 50 noise cells, and no outcome of the proposed test justifies the size tilt.

1. The mechanism does not match the trades. All 928 in-sample entries of the gold Asian-range sleeve fall between 06:00 and 11:59 UTC (range ends 07:00 London, entries until 12:00 London). No US release is in that window, so the 'data posts' are German, UK and euro-area numbers, not 'a release that moves the dollar and yields'. Those numbers matter far more for EUR and GBP, and that is exactly where the designer's own high-powered replication (14,245 FX London-open breakouts) shows a gap of 0.03 R, against 0.39 R on gold. I read that as a failed replication where the mechanism should be strongest.

2. Multiplicity. Resampling the sleeve's own in-sample R with a random 31 % flag, the best |t| among 50 null cells has a median of 2.55, and 61 % of such searches reach 2.4. The sleeve is fat-tailed (the 5 best trades are 55 % of its in-sample profit), so any flag that catches three of them looks large.

3. A visible gold reaction before the break is bad, not good. Breakouts whose previous 30 minutes contain an abnormal one-minute move (top third, n 309) earn -0.14 R against +0.27 R for the other 619 (difference -0.42 R, t -3.1, worse in 8 of 8 years). This is my own exploratory cell and it does not refute the claim (news jump good, no-news jump bad is still possible). It does mean either the flagged posts did not move gold, or they must overcome a negative base rate.

4. The validation step is not decisive and the tilt has negative expected value. Simulated on the sleeve's R distribution, the pass rule (gap at least +0.15 R, mean above 0, 3 of 4 years) passes 18 % of the time with no effect and 49 % with a true gap of 0.20 R, a likelihood ratio of about 2.7. A pass moves 9 % to roughly 21 %. A 1.5x / 0.5x tilt on a noise flag cuts the sleeve's effective bets from 116 to about 88 a year (about -13 % risk-adjusted). A real half-strength effect adds about +20 %, so break-even needs about 39 % belief, which no result of step 2 delivers.

It also adds no trades and no winning days, and at best lifts one sleeve of eleven. The gold sleeve's validation period has already been read many times (lab/r2/tracks/gold2/finalize_preval.py says 'no clean test is left'; results/val_access.log shows repeated reads). reviews.name: Reader on unscheduled news: follow a jump only when confirmed, new, material news is found behind it
reviews.fatal_flaw:
The first experiment cannot detect the effect it hypothesises, and nothing measured so far says the effect exists on ordinary days.

1. Power. In-sample, the 60-minute return after a 5-sigma one-minute jump has a standard deviation of 30 bp on gold, 42 bp on us100 and 17 bp on eurusd, about 35 bp pooled. A class of 80 events bunched on perhaps 40-50 distinct days (one headline moves several markets) has a standard error near 5 bp. Passing at p <= 0.01 therefore needs an observed mean of about 11 bp net. If the true edge is the designer's own bar (4-5 bp net), the chance of passing the first leg is about 10 %, and lower once the two other legs are added. The expected result is 'fail' or 'inconclusive' whether or not the idea is true. A properly powered test (80 % power for 5 bp) needs roughly 500 independent events, which is 1.5 to 3 years of forward logging. The 150-event demo rule does not fix this.

2. The designer's own in-sample numbers already say the plain version is a rare-big-day harvest: +6.7 bp gross falls to +1.5 bp (t 1.1, about the cost) without 10 days of 609, and to zero per market without its 5 best days. That is the payoff the lab's trend sleeves already collect.

3. Direct contrary evidence from the lab's own post-cutoff test. On presidential posts, the dominant unscheduled political source of 2026, the Nasdaq moves 5 bp in the called direction before post + 2 minutes and gives it back afterwards. This idea enters at jump + 2 minutes and bets on continuation.

4. The cited literature is real but thin for this use. Xiao, Yin and Zhao (2020) do find momentum after unscheduled-news jumps on US broad-market funds, with a paid news database. A 2025 follow-up by Xiao on fund data reports no significant momentum or reversal for unscheduled news. The other papers concern individual shares, not the most-watched markets in the world.

5. Test design defects. Shuffling labels within market ignores same-headline clustering across the six markets, so p-values are too small; the shuffle should be by day. 'Beats the keyword flag' has no threshold and is a coin flip. The Telegram stamp is the post time of a free relay, not the time the news reached professional screens.

Unconditionally there is nothing to lean on: after all 5-sigma jumps the 60-minute follow-through is +0.65 bp gross on gold (n 5,452, t 1.6), +1.2 bp on us100 (n 3,928, t 1.8) and -0.3 bp on eurusd (n 5,016). After the historical spread that is -1.1 to -1.7 bp, with 42-46 % winners.
reviews.strongest_point: It is the only honest way to test a language model at reading: strictly post-cutoff data, one frozen prompt, one batch, a closed label instead of a price forecast, a best-days-removed condition, and a no-retry kill rule, for about 20 USD. The source is real: the public squawk page is reachable with a plain request and stamped to the second. The designer already priced it at 4 % and published the numbers that undermine it.
reviews.better_variant: Do not spend four days on a batch whose answer is known in advance. If the lead wants this question kept open, run it as a zero-risk logger inside the live robot: record every jump, the tape rows before the decision and the model's label, with no order. Pre-register one day-clustered test at 500 class events or 150 distinct days, whichever comes later. Restrict it to gold, us100 and eurusd, whose price files the lab already holds. It costs a few dollars a month and gives an answer in about two years.

ideas.name: The League: permanent paper twins, real money only on evidence dated after the freeze, supplied by a rate-limited AI research loop
ideas.pitch: Every rule (the eleven live ones, rules the lab knows are dead, new rules the AI writes, even the language model's own calls) runs for ever as a paper twin on the broker's real quotes, and its record only counts from the day its code was frozen. The AI works every night as researcher and auditor, never as trader; a plain algorithm with pre-declared statistics moves real risk, and the honest speed is a few small probation seats a year and a full promotion only after years, not a change a day.
ideas.mechanism: No new counterparty: the sleeves keep being paid by whoever pays trend and breakout followers (hedgers, slow adjusters, forced liquidations). The league wins against the one opponent that reliably takes a retail quant's money: his own selection. Evidence from this lab: the nine round-2 ideas sent to validation kept on average about 0.3 of their in-sample expectancy (median about 0.4): the two rules taken from published work with a stated mechanism (noise area, opening-candle momentum) kept 80-125 %, the crypto rules 15-45 %, and three kept nothing (release premium, gold squeeze, crypto session). With about 1,500 trials already run, the best of 1,500 pure-noise rules shows t = 3.35 on average (3.7 at 5,000 trials), so in-sample t no longer separates signal from luck. Outside evidence agrees (McLean-Pontiff: -26 % out of sample, -58 % after publication; Gencay 2026: every LLM-discovered strategy rejected once leakage and trial count were controlled). The advantage persists because a record dated after the freeze cannot be overfitted, remembered by a language model or competed away by faster players: it is a property of the process, not of the market. Upside: in my simulation (11 sleeves, 3 secretly dead) knowing exactly which are dead is worth +0.3 Sharpe, while each truly independent live sleeve added multiplies Sharpe by sqrt((n+1)/n), about +6 % each: discovery is worth more than re-weighting, but it is rare. Speed limit, the core fact: evidence grows as n x s^2 (s = mean/sd of a trade's R). t >= 2 needs 4/s^2 trades; an anytime-valid evidence meter of 20 (a betting martingale, valid although the user looks every evening: a worthless rule ever reaches 20 with probability at most 5 %) needs about 6/s^2. Lab sleeves have s = 0.08-0.19 in sample and about 0.03-0.10 in validation, so one sleeve with annual Sharpe 1 needs 4 to 6 years and Sharpe 2 needs 1 to 1.5 years; the whole portfolio at its validation level (0.079 R per trade, annual Sharpe about 1.5 on in-sample trade shapes) needs about 1.7 years for t >= 2 and 2.5 years for the meter, and more than 6 years if the truth is half of validation. Hence the design. Bench (paper): any frozen rule, every admission counted. Quarantine (60 trading days or 50 trades): implementation only, no P&L criterion. Probation (real money, quarter unit, all probation seats together at most 20 % of portfolio risk): in-sample criteria with t >= 3.0, the lead's single validation look, quarantine passed, and the pooled paper record of all AI-generated seats positive over at least 3,000 trades. Full unit: the seat's own forward meter >= 20 and admission by e-BH at a 20 % false-discovery rate over all K seats (for K = 30 the first promotion needs a meter of 150, about 10/s^2 trades: roughly 2.5 years at s = 0.15, never for a typical sleeve). Tests that can actually conclude are run on groups (generator, portfolio), where n is large.
ideas.role_of_ai: Language model, never in the order path: (1) auditor every night: reads the twin-versus-live journal, explains anomalies, writes the evening phone report (about 20 calls); (2) researcher, limited by statistics and not by compute: at most 2 new rule families a week of at most 60 configurations, in-sample data only (to 2021), sources ranked by the lab's own base rates: replications of published rules with a stated mechanism first, frozen transfers to new instruments second, free ideas last; every evaluation passes through a wrapper that writes to an append-only, hash-chained ledger before it returns a number, and each freeze is a timestamped commit; (3) adversary: a second agent attacks every finalist (look-ahead, selection, execution) before the freeze; (4) contestant: any 'model as trader' idea (news, charts, a daily risk dial) gets a paper seat, forward-only by construction, so the memory leak cannot occur (1-3 calls per decision). Total about 3,500-4,000 calls a month. Plain algorithm: replays each day's MT5 one-minute bid/ask history through every frozen rule, computes paper fills, evidence meters and e-BH, applies promotion, demotion and the cost check, and sends the orders of live seats.
ideas.instruments: Whatever each rule trades among FP Markets CFDs with free one-minute history: today us100, gold, bitcoin, ether (the eleven sleeves); candidates may add us500, us30, ger40, major FX. Paper seats are free, so breadth on paper is unlimited; real risk on unproven seats is capped at 20 % of the portfolio's risk.
ideas.trades_per_day: Live: unchanged at first (4-5 a day from the eleven). Paper: 30-100 a day across 20-40 twins. New live trades only through promotion: at most +0.5 to +1.5 a day per year, at quarter size.
ideas.edge_vs_cost: The league adds no gross edge of its own. Admission to the bench: pre-registered gross edge >= 3 x the measured round-trip cost (>= 2.4 bp us100, 3.3 gold, 2.6 eurusd, 12 bitcoin, 45 ether). Expected forward value of an admitted candidate after the lab's own shrinkage: in-sample 0.10-0.20 R x 0.35 retention x about 0.7 for picked-over ground = +0.02 to +0.05 R per trade, about +1 to +2 bp net where 1 R is 35-60 bp (us100, gold), costs already paid: positive but slow to prove. To be confirmable forward within about two years a rule needs a net edge of at least 0.15 sd of its own trade result and 150+ trades a year: about 4 bp net on a one-hour us100 or gold trade (cost 0.8-1.1, sd 28), 6.6 bp on bitcoin (cost 4, sd 44), 1 bp on eurusd (cost 0.85, sd 7); the validated us100 sleeves sit at 0.07-0.10, so money on such rules always rests partly on priors. If every probation seat were worthless the drag is bounded: 20 % of risk x -0.02 R x 1,350 trades = about -5 R a year against +50 to +100 R expected from the portfolio.
ideas.first_experiment: Stage 0, retro-league, in-sample only (2-3 days of work, no API cost): regenerate by year the trades of the logged gold and index configurations (several hundred of the 1,343 logged; the trial logs do not store yearly results), apply the admission gate with data to end-2018 only, score 2019-2021. Pass: admitted rules earn > 0 net with family-clustered t >= 2 and beat the rejected ones; the ratio of 2019-21 to pre-2019 expectancy becomes the pre-registered shrinkage factor. It is biased upward (families were chosen knowing all of 2013-2021), so it is a one-sided kill test: ratio <= 0 means the gate selects noise and the generator is not built. Stage 1, forward shake-down (60 trading days; 5-8 days of work because the bridge and a first twin exist in lab/live_ai/pont.py and lab/live/ea_twin.py; 10-15 USD a month for the report): twins of the eleven, 8 known-dead control rules from the lab's graveyard (release premium, gold squeeze, crypto session, 15-minute opening range, pivot bounce, Bollinger fade, end-of-day momentum, dip-buying) and a coin-flip twin of each sleeve (same times, random side). Pass/fail fixed in advance, none on P&L: (a) at least 95 % of twin trades match the backtest engine re-run on vendor data for the same days, median absolute difference <= 0.05 R; (b) signal count inside the 95 % Poisson band (270 +/- 33 for 4.5 a day); (c) spread measured at signals within +/- 25 % of the cost model, else the cost table is rewritten. No P&L conclusion is allowed at day 60: a losing quarter has probability 23 % with the edge intact. Stage 2, months 3-24 (40-80 USD a month): generator test on all AI-generated seats admitted, none removed: pass if the pooled, day-clustered t >= 2 and the mean >= +0.03 R per trade. Power with 30 seats (180 trades a year each, design effect 2.5): 25-31 % if the truth is +0.03 R, 58-70 % if +0.05 R, at 18-24 months. I state the low power on purpose: no design makes it higher.
ideas.kill_rule: (1) Stage 0 ratio <= 0: no generator. (2) Twins cannot reproduce the backtest (match < 95 %) after two repairs: the league's numbers mean nothing, stop. (3) Known-dead controls earn more than +0.03 R per trade on paper after 2,000 trades: paper fills are too kind, all promotions suspended. (4) At 24 months and at least 5,000 forward paper trades, pooled net mean of the AI-generated seats <= 0: nightly generation is switched off for good (probability about 84 % if they only pay costs, 50 % if exactly break-even, 6 % if they are worth +0.03 R); the league continues as auditor only. (5) A seat is never demoted for losing inside its pre-registered evidence horizon (a dead sleeve is negative after 250 trades half the time, a live one 19 % of the time: 2.6 to 1 is not evidence); it is demoted at once if its measured cost exceeds half its validated gross edge, if its signal count leaves the Poisson band two months running, or if live minus twin exceeds 0.05 R per trade over 50 trades. (6) API above 150 USD a month two months running: one family a week.
ideas.differs_from_failed: The three blind tests showed the model cannot pick trades from sheets, charts or posts; here it does none of that: it writes and attacks code, and whatever it produces is judged only on data that did not exist when the code was frozen, so the leak (year recognised from price sheets 55 %, from charts 69 %) is irrelevant by construction. It is not a rule family and not a learned filter: nothing is fitted on forward data, so it cannot pass in sample and fail validation. The failed rules become useful as negative controls that calibrate paper fills. Unlike day-locking or exit reshaping it does not try to manufacture winning days; it changes what is traded only when evidence allows.
ideas.holding_time: Each rule keeps its own (minutes to two days). The league reviews monthly; probation after 2-3 months of quarantine and a positive pooled paper record; full promotion on horizons of two years or more.
ideas.data_needed: MT5's own one-minute bid/ask history of each day from the user's terminal (free) for the nightly replay; vendor one-minute history to 2021 for in-sample work and for the parity check; public arXiv / SSRN listings for the literature queue. The forward test needs no history: it starts the day a rule is frozen; a private git remote timestamps each freeze.

ideas.name: Three clocks: a risk engine that learns costs in weeks and edges in years, and refuses every faster adaptation (a discipline, not an edge)
ideas.pitch: Let the robot adapt each quantity only as fast as it can really be learned: costs, fill quality and signal frequency in weeks, the size of the bets and the sleeve weights over years through heavy shrinkage, with a loss ladder written in advance for the day everything looks bad. My in-sample checks show that the popular forms of adaptation (chasing recent winners, volatility-state sizing, stopping after losses, bandits) add nothing on these sleeves, so the engine deliberately leaves them out.
ideas.mechanism: Nobody new is on the other side; the gain is in not paying spread on sleeves whose edge is smaller than their true cost and in not destroying a real edge by reacting to noise. Fast clock (weeks): the lab's cost frames carry an almost constant spread at the sleeves' entry minutes (coefficient of variation 0.00-0.09 in the 2020-21 in-sample frames: 0.26 bp us100, 2.9 bp bitcoin, 12.9 bp ether), yet the sleeves enter by construction on volatility bursts (a 6-sigma Nasdaq minute, the 09:34 candle, a breakout close), and the ether spread is known only within a factor of four (1.16 to 4.32 USD). In R units the crypto sleeves, about 60 % of all trades, stand only 2.5 to 3.6 times above their modelled cost (the ridge-filtered bitcoin breakout about 7; computed from the lab's quoted validation expectancy and in-sample stop distances), while us100 and gold stand above 5. Three sleeves (the two on ether and bitcoin-follows-Nasdaq) lose their safety margin if the real cost at signal time is 25-35 % above the model and turn negative near 2.5 to 3 times. The spread at each signal is observable without trading; 60 signals pin it down. Slow clock (years): the size of the bets, which is the lever that matters when only the percentage counts. On in-sample trade shapes re-centred to the validation mean, risk 0.5 % per trade gives about +57 % a year if validation is right, +22 % if the truth is half, -5 % if there is no edge; 1 % gives +122 %, +34 %, -19 %; 2 % gives only +17 % at half edge: over-betting. After a full year the standard error of the measured edge is still 0.65 of the validated edge itself, so with a prior centred on half of validation a +100 R year justifies moving from 0.50 % to about 0.61 %, a flat year to 0.39 %, a -100 R year to 0.16 %. Sleeve weights by Bayesian shrinkage gain +0.03 Sharpe in year 1 and +0.15 by years 3-5 in simulation with the correct prior (an oracle gains +0.3). What does not adapt, and why: fewer than half the days win even with the edge intact (45 % in validation), a losing month is under 2 to 1 against the robot, a losing year about 8 to 1 (7 % with the edge, 52 % without).
ideas.role_of_ai: None in the decision path. Plain algorithm: logs bid and ask at every signal, pairs each live fill with its paper twin, updates the cost table, applies the gate with hysteresis, the shrinkage formula and the ladder. Language model: one call a day for the evening report in plain language (what traded, measured cost against model, where each clock stands); it may propose a new threshold only as a new pre-registered version, never by editing a live one.
ideas.instruments: us100, gold, bitcoin, ether (the eleven sleeves). The cost clock matters for bitcoin and ether; the bet-size clock and the ladder act on the whole portfolio.
ideas.trades_per_day: 4-5 as today; 3-4 if the gate halves or switches off one to three crypto sleeves. It adds no trades.
ideas.edge_vs_cost: No new gross edge. Cost in R per trade (task costs, in-sample stop distances): 0.013-0.015 R on us100 (0.8 bp on a stop of about 60 bp), 0.012-0.020 R on gold, 0.016-0.029 R on bitcoin (4 bp on 150-280 bp), 0.043-0.060 R on ether (15 bp on 250-375 bp). Against the lab's quoted validation expectancy this leaves net +0.041 to +0.128 R on the crypto sleeves at modelled cost, about +0.02 to +0.03 R at twice the cost on the three thin ones and about -0.01 to -0.03 R at three times. The gate (on if validated gross >= 2 x measured cost, half risk between 1.5 and 2, off below) therefore moves the portfolio's expectancy by roughly -0.005 to +0.01 R per trade, depending on whether the validated gross edges are taken at face value or halved: it buys a safety margin and a true cost table, not return. The return lever is the bet size, and the ladder is what makes a size bearable: at 0.5 % per trade a 60 R drawdown is -26 % and 90 R is -36 %; at 1 % they are -45 % and -60 %.
ideas.first_experiment: Four weeks, 3-4 days of work, API about 1 USD. Shadow-run the eleven twins on the live feed and log bid and ask at each signal (about 90 signals, about 50 on crypto), with 0.01-lot real fills on bitcoin, ether and gold to measure slippage (a few USD of spread). Table written beforehand: per sleeve, ratio = validated gross expectancy in R (the lead supplies it from 2022-2025) / measured round-trip cost in R; on at >= 2, half risk between 1.5 and 2, off below 1.5, re-read monthly with hysteresis. The clock is useful if the measured cost differs from the model by more than 25 % on at least one sleeve or changes at least one status; otherwise the lab's cost model is confirmed and the gate stays as a silent alarm. In parallel, two single looks by the lead on 2022-2025: (a) the ladder thresholds recomputed on validation trades (mine come from in-sample shapes and ten sleeves); (b) sleeve weights from in-sample posteriors only against equal risk: adopt shrinkage weights only if Sharpe is higher and the worst drawdown no deeper, otherwise equal risk for good.
ideas.kill_rule: Gate: if it flips the same sleeve more than twice in six months it is following noise: freeze that sleeve's status on the six-month mean. Weights: dropped if the single validation look does not beat equal risk. Ladder, in R at one R per trade (weekly block bootstrap of in-sample trades re-centred to 0.079 R): within 12 months a drawdown of 40 R or more happens with probability 47 % with the edge intact (91 % with none), 60 R 13 % (65 %), 90 R 1.7 % (29 %), a negative year 7 % (52 %), a negative two-year total 1 % (51 %). So: nothing shorter than a quarter triggers anything; -60 R from the peak or a negative calendar year: risk halved; -90 R or a negative two-year total: paper only, the twins keep running, risk restored when the paper portfolio has recovered half of the drawdown. The bet size moves once a year by the shrinkage formula and never by more than +/- 25 %.
ideas.differs_from_failed: It is not a forecast, not a filter learned from prices (that worked on crypto only) and not an exit or day-lock trick: it adapts to measured costs and to accumulated evidence, the two inputs the earlier rounds treated as fixed. It also records as negative results, before anyone builds them, the adaptive schemes that the in-sample data reject.
ideas.holding_time: Unchanged per sleeve (minutes to two days). Cost gate re-read monthly, weights and bet size yearly, ladder continuous.
ideas.data_needed: Live bid/ask at signal times and the account's own fills from MT5 (free; four weeks are enough for the cost reading); per-sleeve validation expectancy and trade lists (the lead has them) for the gate ratios and the ladder bootstrap; nothing else.

dropped_by_designer: Re-weighting sleeves on recent results (winner-chasing, strategy momentum): in sample a sleeve's monthly result has no memory (pooled lag-1 autocorrelation -0.04, 769 sleeve-months); on volatility-equalised sleeves 'top half by trailing 6 / 12 / 3 months' gives Sharpe 2.22 / 1.92 / 1.52 against 2.08 for equal weights, top-minus-bottom t = 1.1 / 0.0 / -1.1.

Bandits / Thompson sampling over the eleven: in simulation Sharpe 1.59 against 1.88 for equal weights in year 1 and still behind after 5 years; arms that differ by 0.05 R with sd 1.4 R need thousands of trades each to be told apart.

Volatility-state sizing (more risk when the stop distance is below its one-year median): the raw effect is large (0.22 R against 0.06 R, day-clustered t 4.7, 8 of 10 sleeves) but it is a rescaling of R, dispersion rises in the same proportion: Sharpe 2.83 and 2.98 for the two pre-declared sizings against 2.93, placebo with shuffled states 2.82; its cousin, the gold volatility-contraction breakout, failed validation.
Volatility targeting of the whole portfolio on realised P&L: absolute daily P&L has no memory (lag-1 autocorrelation -0.01); Sharpe 2.71 against 2.84.
Sleeve risk parity, and halving the crypto cluster: +0.11 Sharpe (95 % interval -0.15 to +0.38) and -0.07; the sign changes across sub-periods.

Equity-curve trading (cut or stop after losses): mean daily result inside a drawdown deeper than 10 R was 1.07 R against 0.68 R outside; a 40 R drawdown within a year has probability 47 % with the edge intact.
Co-firing as a regime signal (other sleeves triggered in the last 24 hours): correlation with the trade's R -0.02, sign differs by sleeve.
Demoting single sleeves on their own P&L ('t below -1.5 after 100 trades'): in a year it removes 11 % of dead sleeves and 3 % of live ones; after 10 years 32 % and 5 %.

Fast promotion on a few weeks of paper results ('promote what worked this month'): with 15 trades the standard error of a per-trade Sharpe is 0.26 against effects of 0.05-0.15; it would promote noise.

Regime classifier on price features (hidden Markov, trend versus range, day type): same information as the learned filter that found nothing on us100, ger40 and gold (out-of-fold PF 0.91-1.09); eight in-sample years hold only a handful of regime episodes.

Slow 'crypto bull phase' switch for the five crypto sleeves: plausible from the lab's year pattern, but every in-sample crypto year was positive, so it could only be fitted on the validation years: no honest test exists.

Daily language-model risk dial (reads calendar and news, sets tomorrow's risk): three negative blind tests, and the paired forward difference is only a fraction of P&L, so it needs years; kept as a paper seat in the league, nothing more.

Yearly re-fit of the crypto ridge filter: the one place a learned model beat its baseline out of sample, but the expected gain over the frozen scorecard is small and it sits on the decaying, 2024-dependent crypto cluster; offered as a paired twin (frozen against re-fitted), not as an idea.

Nightly re-optimisation of rule parameters: the rules already normalise by rolling volatility (14-session sigma, 20-session median, 20-day sigma) and the protocol demands flat neighbourhoods; it only adds trials (the best of 5,000 noise trials shows t = 3.7).

Execution learning (limit entries, waiting for a tighter spread): at a market-maker CFD a buy limit fills only when the ask comes down to it (adverse selection, no queue advantage), and breakout sleeves earn on the few runaway trades a passive order misses (top 5 % of trades = 92 % of profit on the crypto breakout).

Reinforcement learning or an online deep learner on prices: same signal-to-cost wall as the gradient-boosting micro test (right 51-56 %, 55-75 % needed), with far more hidden trials and no audit trail.
